Description: Wihtlaeg reigned in 374 AD as paramount King of the Angles in the Jutland peninsula and Angeln, ancestral patriarch of the royal Mercian house of Iclingas recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. Dominating the stormy maritime coastlands between the Baltic and North Seas, Wihtlaeg was an indomitable warrior-king who successfully defended his homeland against early Danish incursions. Mastering naval architecture, he oversaw the construction of swift, seaworthy clinker raiding vessels. Forging maritime alliances with neighboring Saxons, Wihtlaeg launched aggressive cross-North-Sea raiding flotillas targeting the vulnerable Saxon Shore forts of Roman Britain, laying the foundational naval pathways for the eventual Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain. During the tumultuous conflicts of the late fourth century, he served as an indispensable pillar of tactical stability and frontline command. Drilling his warrior retinues daily and inspecting ramparts, he personally verified spearheads, shield-bosses, and sentry postings, eliminating indiscipline through exemplary leadership. When battle was joined, his cold composure under fire directed devastating counter-thrusts that shattered hostile formations at critical junctures. Placing the preservation of his folk and territorial sovereignty above all mortal ambition, this dedicated warlord stood as an unbreakable bastion of defiance.

Motivations: Repel Danish southern territorial thrusts to secure the ancestral homeland in Angeln
Lead grand flotillas across the North Sea to raid and prospect permanent settlements in Britain
Values: The storm-tossed seas are trials for the brave; idle cowards deserve no iron in hand
Tribal destiny lies not in starving upon barren heaths, but in carving kingdoms across the water
Fears: Fears sudden Arctic nor'easters wrecking the main expeditionary fleet against uncharted reefs
